_about: PRO rewrite pass 12: era-3 scenes 118-150 in play order.

scenarios.title: The Family Schedule
scenarios.text: Your kids' games and your schedule are in a war you keep losing: soccer on Saturdays, recitals on Thursdays, and a road trip every other weekend of the fall.

choices.label: Make every game you can
choices.result: Every game you can make, even if it means a red-eye and a nap in the car. The kids look for you in the stands, and find you more often than not.

choices.label: Plan the season on one calendar
choices.result: One big calendar on the kitchen wall, with every game, recital and road trip in different colors. It's chaos made visible, and it helps.

choices.label: Watch the videos after practice
choices.result: The videos, watched in the locker room after practice, every one. It's not the same, and the kids know it, and they send them anyway.

scenarios.title: The Family Business Dispute
scenarios.text: A business with relatives in it is turning into a family fight: a cousin wants to expand, an uncle wants out, and everyone wants you to decide at Thanksgiving.

choices.label: Bring in a mediator
choices.result: A professional mediator, hired before the holiday. It's expensive and it works, and Thanksgiving is merely awkward instead of explosive.

choices.label: Step back from the business
choices.result: Out of the business, and into the family. You sell your share to the cousin, and dinner that year is the warmest in years.

choices.label: Take charge of it
choices.result: In charge, for a season, making the hard calls yourself. It's a lot of work, the business steadies, and a few people stay mad.

scenarios.title: The New Home
scenarios.text: Your family has outgrown the house: three kids, two dogs, one bathroom that everybody fights over every morning, and a garage completely full of kicking nets.

choices.label: Let the kids choose their rooms
choices.result: A bigger house, and the kids pick their rooms first, loudly. The move is chaotic and happy, and the dogs love the yard.

choices.label: Add a room instead
choices.result: An addition instead of a move, built over the offseason. The kids keep their school and their friends, and you keep your street.

choices.label: Make it work another year
choices.result: One more year in the small house, creatively. It's crowded and warm, you build bunk beds yourself, badly, and {sibling} helps.

scenarios.title: The Business Partner's Exit
scenarios.text: A partner wants out of a business you built together: the restaurant, the dealership, the start-up, whichever it is. He's tired, and he wants his money back by spring.

choices.label: Buy him out fairly
choices.result: A fair buyout, with lawyers and a handshake at the end. He leaves happy, and the business is all yours now, for better and worse.

choices.label: Sell it together
choices.result: You both sell, and split it evenly down the middle. The business goes to new owners, and the friendship stays completely intact.

choices.label: Run it alone
choices.result: Alone, with his share bought on a payment plan. It's more work than you thought, and you learn a great deal about payroll.

scenarios.title: The Family Financial Decision
scenarios.text: You and {love_interest} disagree about a major purchase: a lake house, two hours away, that one of you loves and the other thinks you'll never use.

choices.label: Let {love_interest} decide
choices.result: Their decision, fully. It's the right call, and you know it the first weekend you sit on the dock together.

choices.label: Sleep on it for a month
choices.result: A month, before anyone decides anything at all. The decision makes itself in the end, and neither of you has to win the argument.

choices.label: Make your case
choices.result: Your case, made carefully at the kitchen table with a spreadsheet and a chart. You win, and the house is very quiet for a whole day.

scenarios.title: The Business Reputation
scenarios.text: A customer's angry post about your business has been shared all over town, with your face in the picture. Your name is on the sign, so it's your problem now.

choices.label: Fix the problem
choices.result: You find out what actually went wrong, fix it, and say so publicly in plain words. A few people unfollow, more come back, and the manager stops dreading Mondays.

choices.label: Call the customer
choices.result: You call the customer yourself. They don't believe it's you at first, then talk for twenty minutes. Their next post is about the phone call.

choices.label: Let the managers handle it
choices.result: You leave it to the managers. They handle it fine, slowly, and for a month people bring it up whenever they recognize you.

scenarios.title: The Next Chapter Conversation
scenarios.text: {love_interest} wants to know, over a late dinner, what you picture for life after football. It's a simple question, and you realize you've never answered it out loud.

choices.label: Picture it together
choices.result: The picture, painted together, piece by piece: a town, a porch, a coaching job. It sounds good, and you both go quiet for a while.

choices.label: Each make a list
choices.result: Two lists, written separately and compared over coffee. They overlap more than you thought, and the differences are interesting, not scary.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.result: Not there yet, you say honestly. {love_interest} waits, patiently, and the question comes back every spring, a little warmer each time.

scenarios.title: Contract Year: The Middle Years
scenarios.text: A contract year in your thirties means proving you're not slowing down. The club has a younger kicker on the practice squad, and the general manager mentions it.

choices.label: Train like a rookie
choices.result: All summer, like a rookie: early, hard, hungry. You come back faster than you've been in three years, and the general manager notices.

choices.label: Show them the numbers
choices.result: Your numbers, shown to the club: as good as ever, better in the cold. They agree, grudgingly, and the conversation changes.

choices.label: Keep it calm at home
choices.result: Calm at home, on purpose: the contract will come or it won't. You sleep well, and your kicks feel easy.

scenarios.title: The New Club at Thirty
scenarios.text: A new club, at thirty-one, and the young players already know your name. Some of them had your poster. One of them asks you to sign his old jersey.

choices.label: Earn it anyway
choices.result: Earned anyway, one practice at a time, as if nobody knew you. The young players respect that more than the poster.

choices.label: Take the young specialists to lunch
choices.result: Lunch, the first week, with every young specialist. By Friday they're asking you everything, and you're the heart of the room.

choices.label: Focus on the job
choices.result: Just the job, quietly, and the rest follows on its own. You sign the old jersey, say very little else, and the young players respect it.

scenarios.title: Kindergarten Morning
scenarios.text: Your youngest's first day of kindergarten is a practice day, and the drop-off is at the exact time of the special teams meeting. There's a photo planned by the front door.

choices.label: Ask to come in late
choices.result: An hour, asked of {coach} and granted instantly. You're there for the photo, the backpack and the wave at the classroom door.

choices.label: Drop off and race to the meeting
choices.result: Drop-off at seven-forty and the special teams meeting at eight-fifteen, barely. You're out of breath, sweaty and very happy all morning.

choices.label: Go to practice
choices.result: Practice, and the whole story at dinner, told twice by a very proud five-year-old. You hang on every word and ask for it a third time.

scenarios.title: The Kid's Team
scenarios.text: Your kid's youth team needs a coach, and every parent at the meeting slowly turns to look at you. You've never coached nine-year-olds in your life.

choices.label: Coach the team
choices.result: Head coach, with a whistle and a clipboard. It's the most stressful thing you do all year, and the most fun.

choices.label: Be an assistant
choices.result: Assistant coach, which means snacks, cones and a lot of encouragement. It's perfect, and your kid is delighted you're there every week.

choices.label: Cheer from the stands
choices.result: The stands, loud and proud, every Saturday morning. Another parent coaches, and you bring the orange slices and the folding chairs.

scenarios.title: The Anniversary Trip
scenarios.text: You and {love_interest} have planned an anniversary trip for months, flights and all, and then the club schedules a mandatory minicamp on the same four days.

choices.label: Ask to miss a day
choices.result: A day off minicamp, asked for and granted, grudgingly. You catch the last flight, and the trip is three days instead of four.

choices.label: Move the trip
choices.result: The trip, moved a week later, with a lot of rebooking and one angry airline. It's a little less magical, and still wonderful.

choices.label: Go to minicamp
choices.result: Minicamp, and a promise of next year instead. {love_interest} understands, and you can tell they're tired of having to understand.

scenarios.title: The Marriage Counselor
scenarios.text: You and {love_interest} decide to see a counselor together, before anything's wrong. It was their idea, and you agreed faster than either of you expected.

choices.label: Commit to it
choices.result: You commit to it, every other Tuesday, even in season. It's the best thing you do for the marriage, and you say so out loud.

choices.label: Go every other week
choices.result: You go every other week when the schedule allows. It helps, and you learn how differently you two remember the same arguments.

choices.label: Try it once
choices.result: You go to one session to see what it's like. It's harder than practice, and you leave unsure whether you'll go back.

scenarios.title: The Second Business
scenarios.text: You're considering a second business while the first is still finding its feet: a gym this time, with your name on the door and a partner who talks very fast.

choices.label: Wait a year
choices.result: A year's wait, until the first business is steady. The fast-talking partner finds someone else, and you're relieved by spring.

choices.label: Do both
choices.result: Both, at once. You don't sleep much for months, and the gym opens in June to a line around the block.

choices.label: Ask your first partner
choices.result: Your partner in the first business, asked honestly over lunch. The answer is 'please not yet', and you listen to them.

scenarios.title: The Commercial Shoot
scenarios.text: A national commercial shoot, two days in a studio with a famous director who wants you to act: a scene where you kick a ball into a moving truck.

choices.label: Go for it
choices.result: All in on the acting, with real feeling. The commercial is silly and everywhere, and your teammates quote it at you for a year.

choices.label: Ask for fewer lines
choices.result: Fewer lines, you suggest politely, and more kicking. The director agrees after a long pause, and it works much better on screen.

choices.label: Do one take and leave
choices.result: One stiff take, and you leave for the airport. The director uses it anyway, and it shows in every frame.

scenarios.title: The Late-Night Show
scenarios.text: A late-night show wants you as a guest during the bye week. The producers want a funny kicker story and maybe a kick on the studio set.

choices.label: Be funny
choices.result: You're funny, mostly at your own expense. The clip goes around the league, and the whole locker room does the bit back at you for a month.

choices.label: Bring one story
choices.result: You bring one good story about your first pro camp and tell it well. The host stops laughing long enough to say it was a good story.

choices.label: Decline
choices.result: You decline and spend the bye week at home. The producers book a punter instead, and he's better on television than you'd have been.

scenarios.title: Baby Number Two
scenarios.text: A second child, and the house feels half its size. Everyone is tired, nobody is sleeping, the dog is confused, and the season starts in three weeks.

choices.label: Take the night shift
choices.result: You take the night shifts on your off days. You're exhausted at practice and closer to {love_interest} than you've been in years.

choices.label: Make a plan
choices.result: You make a plan for the season, down to who sleeps when. It works about half the time, which is better than nothing.

choices.label: Ask the grandparents
choices.result: You ask the grandparents to come for a month. Everyone sleeps, and the house is loud and full in the best way.

scenarios.title: The School Play
scenarios.text: Your kid's school play is the night before a road game. They're playing a tree, with two lines, and they've practiced them on you every night for a month.

choices.label: Go to the play
choices.result: The play, front row, and a late flight to join the team. You know both lines by heart, and you mouth them along.

choices.label: Watch the dress rehearsal
choices.result: The dress rehearsal, the afternoon before, front row of an empty gym. Your kid performs the tree just for you.

choices.label: Watch the video on the plane
choices.result: The video, on the plane, twice. Your kid forgives you faster than you forgive yourself, and you never miss the next play.

scenarios.title: The Parent-Teacher Conference
scenarios.text: You go to your first parent-teacher conference, in a tiny chair, and the teacher recognizes you immediately and asks for an autograph for her nephew.

choices.label: Laugh and focus on your kid
choices.result: An autograph, a laugh, and then forty minutes about your kid's reading. You learn things about your own kid you never knew.

choices.label: Ask good questions
choices.result: Good questions, carefully asked, all of them about your kid and none about you. The teacher forgets you kick by the third question.

choices.label: Keep it short
choices.result: A short meeting, and you leave with a list of spelling words to practice. Your kid is thrilled you came at all.

scenarios.title: The Family Dog
scenarios.text: The family dog is getting old: slow on walks, gray in the face, sleeping by the door. The kids have started asking questions you don't know how to answer.

choices.label: Answer honestly
choices.result: Honest answers, at the kitchen table, about getting old and saying goodbye. It's a hard talk and a good one.

choices.label: Find a good book
choices.result: A good book about it, found by you and read together at bedtime, twice. The kids ask better questions after.

choices.label: Spend time with the dog
choices.result: More time with the old dog: slow walks, long naps, the good treats. The kids join you on every walk.

scenarios.title: The Partner's New Job
scenarios.text: {love_interest} gets a big job offer of their own, in a city you'd never live in during the season. They're excited, and trying not to show it.

choices.label: Back them all the way
choices.result: You back them all the way and work out the travel later. Your life gets busier and lonelier, and {love_interest} glows every time you call.

choices.label: Make it work together
choices.result: You sit down with a calendar and make a plan that works for both careers. It's complicated and fair, and it holds.

choices.label: Ask them to wait
choices.result: You ask them to wait a year, until your contract is settled. They agree, and something goes quiet between you.

scenarios.title: The Prime-Time Interview
scenarios.text: A national network wants an in-depth interview about your whole career: two days of filming, your hometown, your family, the hard years. It will air before the playoffs.

choices.label: Open up about the hard years
choices.result: The hard years, told honestly on camera. People write to you for weeks, and some of the letters make you cry.

choices.label: Prepare carefully
choices.result: Every answer, prepared and true, rehearsed twice with {best_friend}. It's a strong piece, and you say exactly what you mean on camera.

choices.label: Keep it light
choices.result: Light and funny, nothing heavy at all. It's a nice piece about nothing much, and {parent} likes it best of everything.

scenarios.title: The Contract Year Pressure at Home
scenarios.text: Contract year again, and the conversations at home are getting shorter. {love_interest} has stopped asking how practice went, and you've stopped offering anything at all.

choices.label: Talk about all of it
choices.result: All of it, one night after the kids are asleep: the fear, the money, the next city. It's long and hard and the best talk in months.

choices.label: Plan for every outcome
choices.result: A plan for every outcome, written down together: stay, move, retire. It helps, because nothing will be a surprise anymore.

choices.label: Focus on kicking
choices.result: Kicking, only kicking, and home gets quieter. The contract comes in March, and the quiet takes much longer to fix.

scenarios.title: The Family Photo
scenarios.text: The family photo for the team's holiday card, in matching sweaters, and nobody is smiling: the baby is crying, the dog is escaping, and your eldest is furious about the sweater.

choices.label: Make them laugh
choices.result: A ridiculous face, and everyone laughs at once. The photo is chaos and perfect, and the club uses it on the cover.

choices.label: Bribe with dessert
choices.result: Dessert, promised loudly to everyone. They all smile on cue, the photographer thanks you, and the dog stays put for once.

choices.label: Go with the grumpy one
choices.result: The grumpy photo, kept on purpose. It becomes the family's favorite picture of all time, framed in the hallway forever.

scenarios.title: The Kicker You Grew Up Watching
scenarios.text: The kicker whose poster hung above your bed when you were ten is at your game, in a suite, and he sends word that he'd like to meet you after.

choices.label: Meet him
choices.result: A meeting in the tunnel after the game. You tell him about the poster, he laughs, and he signs your shoe like you're the fan.

choices.label: Ask him everything
choices.result: How did he last so long, through all of it? You ask him everything, for an hour in the tunnel, and he answers every question honestly.

choices.label: Shake his hand
choices.result: A handshake and a simple thank-you, nothing more. It's brief, and it's enough, and you call {parent} from the car on the way home.

scenarios.title: The Rule Change
scenarios.text: The league moves the extra-point line back again, the second time in your career. The young kickers in camp are thrilled about it; you've lived through this once already.

choices.label: Adjust your training
choices.result: New distances, added to every practice the next morning. By camp the new line feels normal, and the young kickers are surprised.

choices.label: Study the change
choices.result: The change, studied properly: the angles, the wind off each end zone, the hash marks. You find the edge before anyone else in the league does.

choices.label: Wait and see
choices.result: Wait until camp, you decide, and see how it feels with real snaps. It feels fine, and you're glad you didn't spend the summer worrying.

scenarios.title: The Rookie Who Wears Your Number
scenarios.text: A rookie at another club wears your number and tells a reporter you're the reason he started kicking. The clip is everywhere by morning, and your phone won't stop.

choices.label: Call him
choices.result: Your call reaches him on his cell, and he's speechless for ten full seconds. You wish him luck, and he calls you every season after.

choices.label: Send him a note
choices.result: The best advice you ever got, written on a card and mailed to his locker. He tapes it inside, he says, forever.

choices.label: Smile and keep it
choices.result: A smile, kept to yourself, and the clip watched twice. You don't reach out, and it stays with you all week.

scenarios.title: The Coach You Outlasted
scenarios.text: The head coach who drafted you is fired after a bad season, in a short statement on a Monday. You've outlasted him. It doesn't feel like a win at all.

choices.label: Call him
choices.result: You call him that night. He thanks you for calling, talks about your rookie camp for twenty minutes, and you hear his family in the background.

choices.label: Steady the room
choices.result: You steady the room the next morning, before the rumors start. The new coach hears about it before you meet him.

choices.label: Keep going
choices.result: You keep going, because that's the business, and you've seen it before. You keep his old playbook on a shelf at home, though.

scenarios.title: The Hall of Fame Conversation
scenarios.text: A broadcaster asks, on air, whether you ever think about your legacy. It's a soft question, and it lands harder than he meant it to.

choices.label: Give an honest answer
choices.result: You say you think about the next kick, which is true. Later, in the car, you think about the question for a long time.

choices.label: Talk about the people
choices.result: You talk about the people who got you here: {parent}, your first coach, the holders. The clip is the one your family keeps.

choices.label: Laugh it off
choices.result: You laugh and say you'll worry about it when you're old. Your teammates tease you about it, and the question stays with you.

scenarios.title: The Kicking Records Board
scenarios.text: Your name goes up on the club's kicking records board in the hallway, above two legends. The equipment manager screws in the plaque while you watch.

choices.label: Bring {holder} to see it
choices.result: {holder}, brought to see it, because their name should be there too. {holder} pretends not to care and takes a photo.

choices.label: Aim for the next name
choices.result: The next name on the list, noted carefully. It's three good kicks away, and you start counting them in practice.

choices.label: Take a picture for {parent}
choices.result: A photo of the plaque, sent to {parent}, who prints it out and puts it next to your peewee trophy on the mantel.

scenarios.title: The Halfway Point
scenarios.text: A reporter asks if you think you're halfway through your career. You're thirty-two, it's a fair question, and you have no idea how to answer it.

choices.label: Give a careful answer
choices.result: Focused on this season, you say, which is true. Later, in the car, you think about the question for a long time.

choices.label: Joke about it
choices.result: You hope it's a third, you say, and the room laughs. The clip goes around, and {parent} sends it to everyone he knows.

choices.label: Say you're just starting
choices.result: Just getting started, you say, and you mean it. The column the next day calls you 'defiant', which you like.

scenarios.title: The Club's Ring of Honor Nominee
scenarios.text: Fans start a petition to nominate you for the club's ring of honor while you're still playing. It has forty thousand signatures, and the owner has seen it.

choices.label: Thank the fans
choices.result: Thanks, online and in person at the next home game. The fans cheer loudly, and the petition hits sixty thousand by Monday.

choices.label: Ask them to wait
choices.result: Wait until you're done, you ask the fans kindly. They agree, and it gives everyone something to look forward to.

choices.label: Keep it to yourself
choices.result: A smile, kept to yourself, and back to practice. It means more than you'd ever say out loud, even to {parent}.

scenarios.title: Ten Years
scenarios.text: Ten years in the league. The pension kicks in, the club gives you a watch, and the question arrives with it, uninvited: how many more?

choices.label: Go for more
choices.result: Not done, not close. You tell {coach} and your agent the same thing, and you start the eleventh year angrier than the first.

choices.label: Plan the next five years
choices.result: The next five years, planned with your agent and your family at the kitchen table. Everyone breathes easier, including you.

choices.label: Celebrate with the people who got you here
choices.result: A party for everyone who got you here: coaches, holders, {parent}, {best_friend}. The watch goes around the room twice, and {parent} cries.
